title: Inductive off-diagonal image gives a quasi-affine saturated pullback
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $a:T'\to T$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] between affine $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism from an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume that $f$ is chartwise locally quasi-finite: every representable etale scheme chart $U\to X$ has locally quasi-finite composite $U\to T$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Assume also that $f$ is separated: its diagonal $X\to X\times_TX$ becomes a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $X'=X\times_TT'$, and let $V'\subseteq X'$ be an open subspace represented by a scheme. An open subspace means a subfunctor whose inclusion becomes an open immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose $V'\to T'$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]; over an affine target this means a quasi-compact open immersion into an affine scheme. Let $W\subseteq X$ be the open image of $V'\to X$, so that $|W|=\operatorname{im}(|V'|\to|X|)$; point sets and open images are as in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Put $T''=T'\times_TT'$, with projections $\pi_0,\pi_1$, and let $T^*$ be the open and closed complement of the diagonal. Assume $T^*$ is affine and $b=\pi_1|_{T^*}$ is etale. Put $X''=X\times_TT''$, $X^*=X\times_TT^*$, let $p_i:X''\to X'$ be induced by $\pi_i$, and set $Z=p_0^{-1}(V')\cap X^*$. Then $X'\to T'$ is separated and chartwise locally quasi-finite, and $Z$ is an open subspace of $X^*=X'\times_{T',b}T^*$ represented by the scheme $T^*\times_{T',\pi_0}V'$, with quasi-affine structure map to $T^*$. Suppose the open image $H\subseteq X'$ of $Z\xrightarrow{p_1}X'$ is represented by a quasi-compact scheme. Then $P=W\times_XX'=W\times_TT'$ equals the union $V'\cup H$ as open subspaces of $X'$, is represented by a quasi-compact scheme, and its structure map $P\to T'$ is quasi-affine. Quasi-compactness means every open covering has a finite subcover.

source.place: Tag 03XW (lemma-neighbourhood-scheme), proof, third and fourth paragraphs: induction diagram, omitted hypothesis checks, saturation identity, scheme gluing and quasi-affineness

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-space-separated-lqf-permanence] to $f$ and $T'\to T$: $X'\to T'$ is separated and chartwise locally quasi-finite. On sections over any test scheme, both $X^*$ and $X'\times_{T',b}T^*$ consist of a section $x$ of $X$ and a section $t^*$ of $T^*$ with $f(x)=a\pi_1(t^*)$; this gives the claimed identification, since $a\pi_0=a\pi_1$ on $T^*$. The pullback of $V'\subseteq X'$ along the other projection $X^*\to X'$ is open by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. Its sections are pairs $(v,t^*)$ with the $T'$-coordinate of $v$ equal to $\pi_0(t^*)$, so it is exactly $Z=T^*\times_{T',\pi_0}V'$, represented by a scheme. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-base-change], its map to $T^*$ is quasi-affine.

source.place: Tag 03XW, proof, third paragraph: induction diagram and base-change hypothesis checks

proof.text: Put $Q=V'\times_X X'$. Its sections are pairs $((x,t_0),(x,t_1))$, so the fibre-product universal property identifies $Q$ with $p_0^{-1}(V')\subseteq X''$ and its map to $X'$ with $p_1$. Since $\operatorname{im}(|V'|\to|X|)=|W|$, the last assertion of [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], applied with $G=X'$, says that the point image of $Q\to X'$ is $|P|$, where $P=W\times_X X'$. Associating the same coordinates identifies this pullback with $W\times_TT'$. The assumed decomposition $T''=\Delta(T')\amalg T^*$ pulls back to a decomposition of $Q$: over the diagonal its restriction is $V'$ and $p_1$ is the given inclusion; over $T^*$ its restriction is $Z$. Every field-valued point lies in one of these two pieces, because the inverse images of the two clopen pieces in a field spectrum form a partition. Consequently $|P|=|V'|\cup\operatorname{im}(|Z|\to|X'|)=|V'|\cup|H|$. The open-subspace correspondence of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] now gives $P=V'\cup H$ as open subspaces.

source.place: Tag 03XW, proof, fourth paragraph: saturation identity

proof.text: For any scheme $A\to P$, pulling back $V'$ and $H$ gives open subschemes of $A$ by the definition of open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Their underlying opens cover $A$: [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] identifies them with inverse images of $|V'|$ and $|H|$, whose union is $|P|$ by step 2. Thus these two representable open subfunctors form a Zariski covering of $P$. The algebraic space $P$ is an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space], hence a Zariski sheaf by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. Apply [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] to this two-element family: $P$ is represented by a scheme over $S$. This application uses the stated representability criterion, not merely a theorem that glues algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 03XW, proof, fourth paragraph; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03JH (lemma-subscheme), with schemes.tex Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors)

proof.text: The hypothesis that $V'\to T'$ is quasi-affine, with $T'$ affine, says that $V'$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme, so $|V'|$ is quasi-compact. By hypothesis $|H|$ is quasi-compact. Given any open cover of $|P|$, restrict it to these two opens, take a finite subcover on each, and combine the two finite sets. Since $P=V'\cup H$, they cover $|P|$. Thus the representing scheme $P$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 03XW, proof, first and fourth paragraphs: quasi-compactness

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-space-separated-lqf-permanence] to the open subspace $P\subseteq X\times_TT'$; because $P$ is now a scheme, $P\to T'$ is separated and locally quasi-finite as a scheme morphism. The affine scheme $T'$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $P$ is quasi-compact by step 4, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $P\to T'$ quasi-compact. Its local quasi-finiteness gives local finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type]. All four hypotheses of [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism-of-quasi-finite] now hold for this scheme morphism, so $P\to T'$ is quasi-affine.
